name: null_error_hook
purpose: A single RETF. This is the DATA.OVL initial value of the far error hook g_error_hook (0x5394 = 1000:1232), so file/drive errors that happen before disk_error_hook (1000:2322) is installed are silently ignored. Immediately after it (not a Ghidra function) sit two interrupt handlers installed by init_system: 1000:1233 = INT 24h critical-error handler (STI; push DS,BX; DS=0x1f64; word[0x535c]=1; AL=0 'ignore'; pop; IRET) and 1000:1247 = INT 23h Ctrl-Break handler (STI; CLC; IRET). A second RETF-only hook exists at 1000:2320 (used by 2322/251e to disable recursion) and 1000:25ca is a third hook: print_string(0xa0e0) then wait_key(0), RETF (used while writing save files).

0x535c.name: g_last_dos_error
0x535c.meaning: set to 1 by the INT 24h handler

notes: 1233/1247 handlers decoded from raw bytes (Ghidra left them undisassembled).

name: validate_drive_letter
proto: /* AL=letter */ validate_drive_letter() -> CF=0 ok (AL=upper-cased letter, DL=letter-'A'), CF=1 invalid
purpose: Assembly helper for set_default_drive: upper-cases 'a'..'z', computes DL = AL - 'A' and returns CF clear when the result is within 'A'..'Z', CF set otherwise. Ghidra's C (two ifs, no result) is meaningless because the result is the carry flag.
notes: register-called, not C-callable

name: get_cursor_col
purpose: Returns the current text window's cursor column (byte at g_cur_window_ptr+4, window-relative), zero-extended. Companion of get_cursor_row (1cee). cdecl (plain RET), no arguments.

0x539a.name: g_cur_window_ptr
0x539a.meaning: pointer to current 8-byte text window record

name: set_text_bg
purpose: Sets the background colour of the current text window: g_text_bg = bg & 15 and the window's attribute byte (record +6) gets bg in its high nibble, keeping the foreground nibble. Counterpart of set_text_color (1cca) which sets the low nibble.

name: scroll_window_up
purpose: Scrolls the current text window up by lines text rows: SI = window record, window_pixel_rect (1f77) loads AX,BX,CX,DX with the window's pixel rectangle, SI = -(lines*8) and driver entry 13 (offset 0x27) is called (negative SI = scroll contents upward by that many pixel rows). No callers: put_char has its own inline 8-pixel scroll. Equivalent to scroll_rect (71ca) applied to the current window.
notes: dead code

name: window_pixel_rect
proto: /* SI=window record */ window_pixel_rect() -> AX=x0*8, BX=y0*8, CX=x1*8+7, DX=y1*8+7
purpose: Converts the 4 cell-coordinate bytes of a text window record (x0,y0,x1,y1 in 8x8 cells) into an inclusive pixel rectangle in AX,BX,CX,DX. Used by put_char (window clear/scroll) and scroll_window_up.
notes: register-called

name: backspace_chars
purpose: Erases count characters backwards in the current window for line editing. Does nothing if the cursor is at (0,0) or count==0. With g_cursor_advance temporarily forced to 0: repeat count times { col = get_cursor_col(); put_char(' ') (overwrites the cell under the cursor, where the animated input cursor was drawn, without advancing); if col==0 move to (width = x1-x0, row-1) else move to (col-1, row) }. Then restores g_cursor_advance. The previously typed character is not blanked explicitly; it is covered by the next cursor glyph/typed character (poll_key_with_cursor draws the cursor there).
notes: Callers: read_line, read_text_line (3b1c), read_number (3b9e).

name: to_upper
purpose: Returns c - 0x20 if c is 'a'..'z', else c unchanged (zero-extended to int). Used on every key read by read_command_key so all command letters are upper case.

name: get_time_hash
purpose: Reads the DOS time (INT 21h AH=2Ch: CH=hour, CL=minute, DH=second, DL=1/100 s) and folds it into a 12-bit value: (((CH<<1)<<8 | (CL<<2)) + ((DH<<3)<<8 | DL)) ^ 0x91eb, masked with 0xfff. Every caller immediately passes the result to set_random_seed (207e), i.e. this is the seed source for the game RNG.
notes: shifts are done on 8-bit halves so bits overflow out; only the low 12 bits survive

name: set_random_seed
purpose: Stores seed in g_rand_seed (0x5420), the state word of rand_range. Called with get_time_hash() at start-up/intro and with g_day in one place (deterministic daily seed).

0x5420.name: g_rand_seed
0x5420.meaning: RNG state for rand_range; DATA.OVL initial value 0

name: rand_range
proto: int rand_range(int lo, int hi)  /* pascal: [bp+6]=lo, [bp+4]=hi */
purpose: The game RNG. Advances the state: s = (((s + 0x9248) ROR 3) ^ 0x9248) + 0x11 (16-bit), stores it in g_rand_seed, then returns (s & 0x7fff) % (hi - lo + 1) + lo (unsigned 16-bit modulo, inclusive range). Pascal convention: Ghidra call sites show FUN_2092(hi, lo), e.g. FUN_2092(8,1) is rand_range(1,8). 102 callers across all modules; must be reproduced bit-exactly for identical behaviour.
notes: hi-lo+1 == 0 would divide by zero (never happens in callers)

name: delay_loop
proto: void delay_loop(int speed_index, int count)  /* pascal: [bp+6]=speed_index, [bp+4]=count */
purpose: Busy-wait delay scaled to CPU speed: inner = g_cpu_speed >> g_delay_shift_table[speed_index] (speed_index is added to 0x5426 as a BYTE offset; every caller passes 1, which reads the unaligned word at 0x5427 = 0, so inner = g_cpu_speed); then count outer iterations of inner decrement loops. Loop counters live in g_delay_inner/g_delay_outer. Used by beep (22c0) and a few overlay delays.

0x5426.name: g_delay_shift_table
0x5426.meaning: shift amounts 0,0,1,1,2,2,2,3x7,4,4,4 (DATA.OVL file 0x5436); indexed by byte offset

notes: table semantics uncertain; effectively always shift 0 in practice

name: wait_ticks
purpose: Waits for ticks timer ticks (18.2 Hz) by hooking INT 1Ch. Fast exit: if ticks==1 and g_cpu_speed <= 0xf0 (slow machine) it returns immediately. Otherwise: g_tick_target=ticks, g_tick_count=0; saves the INT 1Ch vector (INT 21h AH=35h) in g_saved_int1c_seg/off; installs the handler at 1000:2159 (STI; push DS,AX,SI; DS=0x1f64; inc word g_tick_count; pop; IRET - it does not chain); spins until g_tick_count >= g_tick_target; restores the old vector (AH=25h). This is the frame timer of the game (animate_wait 3ae6 calls it with 1).

0x5448.name: g_tick_count
0x5448.meaning: ticks elapsed (incremented by INT 1Ch handler at 2159)

notes: Ghidra misses the handler at 2159 (raw bytes fb 1e 50 56 b8 64 1f 8e d8 8d 36 48 54 ff 04 5e 58 1f cf).

name: str_len
purpose: Counts bytes up to the terminating NUL and returns the count. Pascal convention (RET 2), otherwise identical to strlen.

name: play_sweep_noise
proto: void play_sweep_noise(unsigned phase_step, int hold, int count, unsigned threshold, unsigned threshold_step)  /* pascal: [bp+c],[bp+a],[bp+8],[bp+6],[bp+4] */
purpose: PC-speaker effect generated by bit-banging port 61h (the PIT channel 2 is set to divisor 0x003c, ~19.9 kHz, so only the gate bits matter). g_snd_delay_unit = g_cpu_speed/24 (0 if g_cpu_speed < 100). Then count iterations: phase += phase_step (16-bit, wraps); if g_sound_enabled: speaker gate on (61h |= 3) when phase > threshold else off (61h &= 0xfc); threshold += threshold_step; then a delay of hold x g_snd_delay_unit loop iterations. Because phase wraps, this is a square wave whose period is 65536/phase_step iterations and whose duty cycle drifts with the rising threshold (a sweep/buzz). With sound disabled only the delays run (same duration). Speaker gate is cleared at the end. Ghidra shows the five arguments reversed, e.g. FUN_2192(1,0x9c4,60000,1,0x157c) is play_sweep_noise(0x157c, 1, 60000, 0x9c4, 1). Return value is garbage.

0x5454.name: g_snd_delay_unit
0x5454.meaning: g_cpu_speed/24 delay unit for sound loops

0xa9ce.name: g_sound_enabled
0xa9ce.meaning: nonzero = PC speaker sound on (toggled by a command, set to 1 by INTRO)

notes: 24 callers in overlays (spell/combat effects).

name: play_random_tones
proto: void play_random_tones(int step, int total, int max_freq)  /* pascal: [bp+8]=step, [bp+6]=total, [bp+4]=max_freq */
purpose: Burst of random-pitch tones on the PC speaker (damage/hit/trap noise). g_noise_elapsed=0; if g_sound_enabled gate the speaker on. Loop: advance the private LCG g_noise_seed (same formula as rand_range), freq = 100 + seed % (max_freq-99); program PIT channel 2 (port 42h) with divisor 0x1234de/freq; delay step x (g_cpu_speed>>4) loop iterations; g_noise_elapsed += step; repeat while g_noise_elapsed < total. Finally the speaker gate is cleared (always). Ghidra call sites are reversed: FUN_223c(2000,0x640,10) = play_random_tones(10,0x640,2000) (party damage), (500,3000,0x28) = (0x28,3000,500) (trap / party-member hit), (2000,3000,10) = (10,3000,2000) (monster hit).

0x545c.name: g_noise_seed
0x545c.meaning: private LCG state for tone pitches

notes: PIT is reprogrammed even when sound is off (gate stays closed).

name: beep
proto: void beep(unsigned freq, int duration)  /* pascal: [bp+6]=freq, [bp+4]=duration */
purpose: If g_sound_enabled: start_tone(freq). Then delay_loop(1, duration) and stop_tone(). Ghidra shows FUN_22c0(duration,freq), e.g. FUN_22c0(200,0xa5) is beep(165 Hz, 200).

name: start_tone
purpose: If g_sound_enabled (word compare != 0): writes PIT channel 2 divisor 0x1234de/freq (low byte then high byte to port 42h) and opens the speaker gate (port 61h |= 3). The tone continues until stop_tone.
notes: freq 0 would divide by zero

name: stop_tone
purpose: Clears bits 0-1 of port 61h (speaker gate and timer-2 gate off), unconditionally. Returns the new port value.

name: disk_error_hook
purpose: The far error callback installed in g_error_hook; called by the file layer (file_exists, load_file, read_file_region ...) and the overlay manager whenever a file cannot be opened. It implements the original floppy-disk swapping logic. While running, g_error_hook is pointed at the RETF stub 1000:2320 so nested failures are ignored. letter = g_disk_drive_letters[g_cur_disk]. (1) If letter is known (!=0xff), g_cur_disk != g_disk_drive_set and the DOS current drive differs: just set_default_drive(letter), g_disk_drive_set = g_cur_disk, done. (2) Else if letter < 'C' and g_floppy_count > 1: swap A<->B (letter ^= 3), set_default_drive; if g_disk_drive_set != g_cur_disk, record it and return. (3) If letter is a hard-disk letter (>= 'C', != 0xff): force letter 'A', set_default_drive('A'), g_disk_drive_set = 0xff, done. (4) Otherwise prompt: if g_display_mode == 2 (graphics) set_draw_page(0), define_text_window(0, 6,12, 33,13) and fill_rect(40,88, 279,119) in colour 0 (a black message box); g_disk_drive_set = 0xff. In this (GOG) build the prompt itself is patched out: bytes 2405-2409 now do letter = get_current_drive_letter(); JMP 247d, skipping the dead code at 240a-2472 which printed '\nPlease insert the Ultima V Program/Britannia/Player Disk and press drive letter: ' (strings 0x545f..0x549c). Loop while g_disk_drive_letters[g_cur_disk] == 0xff: if set_default_drive(letter) succeeds break; else letter = to_upper(wait_key(0)). If the entry was unknown it is now set to letter ('B' also sets g_floppy_count = 2; when g_cur_disk == 3 and disk 1 is unknown, disk 1 gets the same letter). Finally: mode 0 -> put_char('\n'); mode 2 -> set_draw_page(1), define_text_window(0, 0,0, 39,24), copy_page(1,0) (restore screen from page 1). g_error_hook is restored to 1000:2322 before returning.

0x5394.name: g_error_hook
0x5394.meaning: error callback (2320 = ignore, 2322 = this, 25ca = write-protect message)

0xa9bd.name: g_cur_disk
0xa9bd.meaning: index of the game disk currently required (0..5; 2 and 5 alias 1)

0xa9be.name: g_display_mode
0xa9be.meaning: 0 = text mode, 1 = intro/loading, 2 = graphics mode (affects how prompts are shown)

0xa9c2.name: g_floppy_count
0xa9c2.meaning: number of floppy drives known (2 once drive B is used)

0xa9c8.name: g_disk_drive_letters
0xa9c8.meaning: drive letter for each game disk, 0xff = not yet known (DATA.OVL initial 0)

0x545e.name: g_disk_drive_set
0x545e.meaning: disk index whose drive is currently selected, 0xff = none

notes: Far function (RETF). The Rust port can reduce this to 'all files on one drive'; keep the semantics that a failed open re-tries after the hook.

name: select_disk
purpose: Makes game disk number disk current before accessing its files: disks 2 and 5 are aliased to 1; g_cur_disk = disk; if its drive letter is known, set_default_drive(letter) and g_disk_drive_set = 0xff (so the next error re-evaluates). g_error_hook is set to the ignore stub 2320 during the call and restored to 2322 afterwards (a failed drive change is silently ignored here). Callers use 0 (program), 1/2/5 (Britannia), 3 (player/save) and 4 (intro) before loading overlays, maps and save games.
notes: Ghidra's (param_1 - 0x5638) is 0xa9c8 + disk.

name: load_file_region
proto: void load_file_region(const char *name, void *buf, unsigned count, unsigned offset)  /* pascal: [bp+a]=name,[bp+8]=buf,[bp+6]=count,[bp+4]=offset */
purpose: Reads count bytes (0 = up to 65535) starting at file offset offset from file name into the DGROUP buffer buf, retrying forever until it succeeds. If g_cur_disk == 3 and that disk's drive letter is still unknown, disk_error_hook is invoked first (prompt for the player disk). Then set_default_drive(g_disk_drive_letters[g_cur_disk]) and loop calling read_file_region (7234: open AL=2, lseek if offset != 0, read, close; on failure stores the DOS error in g_last_dos_error, calls g_error_hook and returns 0) until it returns nonzero. Ghidra call sites are reversed: FUN_256e(0,0x100,&0x5c5a,name) = load_file_region(name, g_monster_table, 0x100, 0); FUN_256e(n*0x160,0x160,&0xad14,'BRIT.CBT') loads combat map n. Used for maps, .OOL object lists, NPC/TLK records, save game pieces.
notes: Infinite loop if the file is permanently missing.

name: save_file_region
proto: void save_file_region(const char *name, const void *buf, unsigned count)  /* pascal: [bp+8]=name,[bp+6]=buf,[bp+4]=count */
purpose: Writes count bytes from DGROUP buf to file name (create/truncate, INT 21h 3Ch/40h/3Eh via write_file 7296), with the same disk-3 prompt and drive selection as load_file_region. Loop until the write succeeds: first spin until file_exists(name) returns 1 (each failure calls disk_error_hook, i.e. waits for the right disk), then temporarily set g_error_hook to 1000:25ca (prints '\nYour disk may be write-protected. Try again.\n' and waits for a key) and call write_file; restore hook 2322; repeat if write_file returned 0. Finally restores g_cur_disk to its entry value and re-selects that disk's drive. Call sites (reversed in Ghidra): FUN_25d8(0x1060,0x55a6,'SAVED.GAM') = save_file_region('SAVED.GAM', g_save_game, 0x1060) -- confirms that SAVED.GAM is the DGROUP image 0x55a6..0x6605; FUN_25d8(0x200,0xb21e,'SAVED.OOL'); FUN_25d8(0x100,0x5c5a,name) writes the monster table to a <map>.OOL.

0x55a6.name: g_save_game
0x55a6.meaning: SAVED.GAM memory image (save offset S = DGROUP 0x55a6+S)

notes: write_file's success return is whatever DI held (nonzero in practice).

name: read_command_key
purpose: Blocking key read used by every command prompt. On Tandy video (g_adapter_type==2) sets g_animate_flag=0xff first. Loop: key = to_upper(poll_key_with_cursor()) (animated cursor + 1-tick delay); while no key, and the party is not in a dungeon (g_location < 0x21 or >= 0x80), calls refresh_map_view (5910) so the map keeps animating while waiting. Then translates: if not from the keypad (g_key_from_keypad==0) and key < 5, key += 0xfa (Ctrl-A..Ctrl-D become 0xfb..0xfe so they cannot collide with direction codes); if from the keypad: '1'->0xd4 (End) '2'->4 (S) '3'->0xd6 (PgDn) '4'->1 (W) '6'->2 (E) '7'->0xd3 (Home) '8'->3 (N) '9'->0xd5 (PgUp). Direction codes used throughout the game: 1=West 2=East 3=North 4=South (arrows arrive already translated by read_key).

0x5891.name: g_animate_flag
0x5891.meaning: save 0x2EB: 0 skip animation this frame, 1 animate, 0xff = redraw only

0x5893.name: g_location
0x5893.meaning: save 0x2ED current party location: 0 Britannia/Underworld, 1..0x20 settlement, 0x21..0x28 dungeon, >=0x80 combat

0x538a.name: g_key_from_keypad
0x538a.meaning: last key came from numeric keypad/arrows

notes: 66 callers.

name: print_party_member_line
purpose: Prints one row of the party status window (window 1) for party member index. set_cursor_pos(0,index). If index >= g_party_count: 15 spaces and return. In combat (g_location >= 0x80), if the active combatant g_active_combatant != 0xff, its roster entry (g_combat_roster[active]) has flag 0x80 (is a party member) and its member field == index, put_char(0xfd) switches inverse video on. Prints the name (g_party[index].name, record 0x55a8+index*0x20) padded with spaces to 9 columns. If index == g_active_member: when status is 'D' or 'S' prints ' ' and clears g_active_member to 0xff, else prints 0x1a (the active-member arrow glyph); other rows print ' '. Then print_number(hp, 4, ' '). Status char: outside combat the record's status byte (+0xb: G good, P poisoned, S sleeping, D dead); in combat, if g_combat_roster[index].flags & 0xe1 == 0x81 and its member == index prints 'C' (charmed) instead, then if inverse was switched on it is switched off with another 0xfd.

0x589e.name: g_active_combatant
0x589e.meaning: save 0x2F8: index of combatant whose turn it is, 0xff none

0xba14.name: g_combat_roster
0xba14.meaning: combat participants: +2 flags (0x80 party member, 1/2/4/8 state bits), +3 party index or monster char, +4 monster-table slot, +6 x, +7 y (RAM only)

0x55a8.name: g_party
0x55a8.meaning: character records (save 0x02): name[9], gender, class, status(+0xb), str,dex,int,mp, hp(+0x10), maxhp, exp, level, inn months, +0x18=7, helmet, armor, weaponL, weaponR, ring(+0x1d), amulet, +0x1f

notes: print_number(value,width,pad) appears reversed in Ghidra as FUN_1a3e(0x20,4,hp).

name: print_gold_line
purpose: Writes the gold line of the status window: saves g_cur_window, select_text_window(1), set_cursor_pos(8,7); prints one leading space for each of gold<1000, gold<100, gold<10 (so the number's right edge stays fixed), then ' G:' and print_number(g_gold,1,' '), then spaces until the cursor column exceeds 14; restores the previous window. Also called directly by SHOPPES after a purchase.

name: draw_status_window
purpose: Redraws the whole party/status window (text window 1, right side of the screen). select_text_window(1); print_party_member_line(0..5); set_cursor_pos(0,7); 'F:' + print_number(g_food,1,' '), spaces to column 8. If not in combat and the transport tile is a frigate ((g_transport_tile & 0xf8) == 0x20): 'Ship:' + hull strength g_ship_hull (monster slot 0 value1) plus a space if < 10; otherwise print_gold_line. Then '\n   ' and the date: a space if month<10 and day<10, month '-' day '-' year (width 3, pad '0'), spaces to column 15. set_cursor_pos(6,6): if g_status_icon == 0 draw the empty icon frame (4f3c) else draw_icon_bracket_left (4c2a), put_char(g_status_icon), draw_icon_bracket_right (4cce). Finally select_text_window(2) (the message window). 92 callers: any change to HP/status/gold/food redraws everything.

0x587c.name: g_transport_tile
0x587c.meaning: save 0x2D6 party vehicle tile minus 0x100 (0x1c on foot, 0x10-13 horse, 0x14-17 carpet, 0x20-27 frigate, 0x28-2b skiff)

0x5c5f.name: g_ship_hull
0x5c5f.meaning: monster slot 0 value1 = hull strength of the party's frigate

0x587a.name: g_status_icon
0x587a.meaning: save 0x2D4 glyph shown between the stats and food/gold rows (protection spell etc.), 0 none

name: highlight_party_line
purpose: Toggles a highlight on party row index of the status window: set_color(g_ui_color1) then fill_rect_xor(192, index*8+8, 311, index*8+15). Because it XORs, calling it a second time with the same index removes the highlight; callers always pair the calls (select_party_member, flash_monster, damage_party_member, combat).
notes: Ghidra call FUN_0b86(idx*8+0xf,0x137,idx*8+8,0xc0) is the reversed fill_rect_xor(0xc0, idx*8+8, 0x137, idx*8+0xf).

name: damage_party_member
proto: void damage_party_member(unsigned index, int amount)  /* pascal: [bp+6]=index, [bp+4]=amount */
purpose: Applies amount hit points of damage to party member index with feedback: highlight_party_line(index), play_random_tones(10,0x640,2000), highlight_party_line(index) (un-highlight); hp -= amount; if hp <= 0: hp = 0, status = 'D' (dead) and, if that member was g_active_member, g_active_member = 0xff. Then draw_status_window(). Ghidra shows FUN_2a52(amount, index).

name: damage_whole_party
purpose: For i in 0..5: if i < g_party_count and member i is not dead ('D'), damage_party_member(i, rand_range(1,8)). Used for starvation, bomb traps, lava/poison fields etc. (16 callers).

name: end_of_turn_party_update
purpose: Per-turn upkeep called by the main loops (MAINOUT/TOWN/DUNGEON) and after sleeping. Walks the party: a dead member who is still g_active_member clears it; members that are neither dead nor asleep are counted as active, and poisoned ('P') ones take damage_party_member(i,1). If the hour changed since the last update (g_hour != g_hour_prev): if g_food == 0 print 'Starving!\n' and damage_whole_party, else at hours 6, 12 and 18 subtract the active-member count from g_food (saturating at 0, sub_int_floor 3f54); g_hour_prev = g_hour. add_byte_capped(&g_turn_counter, 1, 0xff). If g_protection_turns is neither 0 nor 0xff decrement it; when it reaches 0 clear g_status_icon and draw_status_window. Finally regeneration_ring_tick (400c: each living member wearing item ',' (44, Regeneration Ring) in the ring slot has a 1/8 chance of +1 HP, capped at max HP, setting g_status_dirty).

0x5880.name: g_hour_prev
0x5880.meaning: save 0x2DA hour at last upkeep (copy of 0x2D9)

0x588b.name: g_turn_counter
0x588b.meaning: save 0x2E5 turns since game start, sticks at 0xff

0x588e.name: g_protection_turns
0x588e.meaning: save 0x2E8 protective spell duration (0 none, 0xff permanent)

notes: Helper protos (pascal, Ghidra reversed): add_byte_capped(ptr,amount,max)=3ef0, sub_int_floor(ptr,amount)=3f54, add_int_capped(ptr,amount,max)=3f14, sub_byte_floor(ptr,amount)=3f36.

name: tile_walkable
proto: int tile_walkable(unsigned char mover_tile, int tile)  /* pascal: [bp+6]=mover_tile, [bp+4]=tile */
purpose: Basic foot passability: returns 1 when the tile's bit in g_impassable_bitmap is clear (byte tile>>3, bit 0x80>>(tile&7)), i.e. 1 = passable. Exception: tiles 0x90..0x93 are passable only when the mover tile is 0x1c/0x1d (the Avatar on foot) or in 0x40..0x4f; for any other mover they return 0. Only called from can_enter_tile.

0x54d4.name: g_impassable_bitmap
0x54d4.meaning: one bit per tile 0..255 (MSB first), set = blocked for walking (DATA.OVL file 0x54e4)

notes: meaning of tiles 0x90-0x93 and 0x40-0x4f movers not identified

name: tile_is_water
purpose: Returns 1 for tiles 0..3 (water depths) and for tiles 0x60..0x6f, else 0. Used by can_enter_tile for water-borne movers and carpets.
notes: 0x60-0x6f group assumed to be water variants (not verified)

name: can_enter_tile
proto: int can_enter_tile(int mover_tile, int tile)  /* pascal: [bp+6]=mover_tile, [bp+4]=tile */
purpose: Movement rule: may an entity drawn with mover_tile step onto map tile? The movement class is g_move_class_table[mover_tile >> 2] (64 bytes at 0x54f4, one per group of 4 tiles; DATA.OVL values: 0x10-13 horse -> 3, 0x14-17 carpet -> 2, 0x20-27 frigate -> 6, 0x28-2b skiff -> 5, 0x2c-2f -> 6, 0x74-77/0x7c-7f -> 2, 0x80-8f (sea monsters) -> 1, 0x94-97 -> 2, 0x9c-9f -> 4, 0xb0-b3 -> 2, 0xd8-df -> 2, 0xe0-e3 -> 10, 0xe8-eb -> 0xff (never moves), 0xec-ef -> 9, 0xf0-f3 -> 2, 0xf4-f7 -> 8, 0xf8-fb -> 7, 0xfc-ff -> 4, everything else incl. the Avatar 0x1c -> 0). Cases: 0 walkers -> tile_walkable; 1 water-only -> tile_is_water; 2 flying/carpet -> tile in 0x60-0x6f, or water, or walkable; 3 horse -> walkable and tile != 0x8f and tile != 4 (swamp); 4 -> not water; 5 skiff -> for tiles 0x34-0x37 the facing bit (8 >> (mover_tile & 3)) of g_water_dir_mask[tile-0x34+16] must be set; otherwise the tile must be water, tiles < 0x60 are then allowed, and tiles 0x60-0x73 need the facing bit of g_water_dir_mask[tile-0x60]; 6 frigate -> tile <= 2 (deep/medium water) only; 7 -> tile == 4 only; 8 -> tile == 5 only; 9 -> tile == 1 only; 10 -> tile == 7 only; class 0xff or anything else -> 0. Callers pass g_transport_tile or a monster's tile as mover and a tile from the view buffer g_view_tiles (0xab02) or the map. Ghidra shows FUN_2c4c(tile, mover).

0x54f4.name: g_move_class_table
0x54f4.meaning: movement class per group of 4 tiles, indexed by tile>>2 (DATA.OVL file 0x5504)

0x5534.name: g_water_dir_mask
0x5534.meaning: allowed skiff facing bits (8=W? 4,2,1) for water-edge tiles 0x60-0x73; tiles 0x34-0x37 alias entries 16-19 (code reaches it as 0x54d4+tile and 0x5510+tile)

notes: Which facing bit corresponds to which direction was not verified.

name: select_party_member
proto: int select_party_member(int allow_zero)  /* pascal; returns 0..5, -1 Esc, -2 '0' */
purpose: Interactive party-member picker used by Ready, Z-stats, New Order, Hole up (guard), shops, spells. In combat, if the current combatant is a party member, its row highlight is toggled off first (highlight_party_line on the roster's member index). draw_prompt_bar('Select:') (4e50: bar across the top line of the screen in g_ui_color2 with the text). sel = 0; loop: if the highlighted row differs from sel, highlight sel. Read keys with read_command_key ignoring anything > '7': '1'..'6' (and < party size) -> sel = digit-1; direction 4 (S) or 2 (E) -> sel = min(sel+1, party_count-1); 1 (W) or 3 (N) -> sel = max(sel-1, 0); Enter or space -> accept; Esc -> sel = -1 accept; '0' -> only if allow_zero, sel = -2 accept. After each key the old highlight is removed when sel changed. On accept: if sel >= 0 un-highlight it, clear_prompt_bar (4e20) and return sel.
notes: add_int_capped(&sel,1,count-1) and sub_int_floor(&sel,1) are 3f14/3f54 (Ghidra args reversed).

name: select_party_member_no_zero
purpose: select_party_member(0): same picker but '0' is not accepted.

name: set_wind_and_draw
proto: void set_wind_and_draw(int dir)  /* pascal; dir -1 = redraw only */
purpose: If dir != -1: g_wind_dir = dir (0 calm, 1 N, 2 S, 3 E, 4 W) and g_wind_timer = 0. Display: nothing if g_location > 0x20 (dungeon/combat) or g_location == 0x19. If g_party_z >= 0x80 (Underworld, z=0xff): instead of text, set_color(g_ui_color1), draw_line(48,184, 152,184) and set_color(g_ui_color2), fill_rect(48,185, 152,191) (blank wind area) and return. Otherwise select_text_window(0), set_cursor_pos(6,23), draw_icon_bracket_left (4c2a), print 'Calm '/'North'/'South'/'East '/'West ' by g_wind_dir then ' Winds', draw_icon_bracket_right (4cce), select_text_window(2). The wind line sits in text window 0 at row 23 (bottom of the screen).

0x5892.name: g_wind_dir
0x5892.meaning: save 0x2EC wind direction 0 calm 1 N 2 S 3 E 4 W

0x5883.name: g_wind_timer
0x5883.meaning: save 0x2DD turns since wind changed (reset to 0 here, incremented by MAINOUT)

0x5895.name: g_party_z
0x5895.meaning: save 0x2EF z/level: 0 Britannia, 0xff Underworld; dungeon level; town floor

notes: Ghidra draw_line/fill_rect args are reversed.

name: random_wind_change
purpose: Called once per map refresh/turn from refresh_map_view (5910). With probability 1/64 (rand_range(0,63)==0) picks a new wind: dir = rand_range(0,4); a result of 0 (calm) is re-rolled while rand_range(0,255) < 0xc0, i.e. calm is only kept 25% of the time it comes up; then set_wind_and_draw(dir).

name: poison_party_member
purpose: If index < g_party_count and the member is not dead: status = 'P' and draw_status_window(). Sleeping members are overwritten to poisoned too.

name: trap_effect
purpose:
Chest/door trap triggered on party member member (callers: Open, Get, Mix reagents failure). play_random_tones(0x28,3000,500). Outside combat the effect is g_trap_type_table[rand_range(0,7)] (table 0,0,0,1,1,2,2,3: acid 3/8, poison 2/8, bomb 2/8, gas 1/8); in combat rand_range(0,1). 0: 'ACID!
' damage_party_member(member, random_damage_1_30()); 1: 'POISON!
' poison_party_member(member); 2: 'BOMB!
' damage_whole_party(); 3: 'GAS!
' poison_party_member(0..5).

name: earthquake_shake
purpose: Screen-shake effect for tremor/earthquake (spells, Blackthorn, towns). copy_page(0,1) (back up the screen to page 1), set_draw_page(1). 8 rounds of: for y = 8,11,..,179: scroll_rect_up (71ca: rect x 8..183, y..y+4, by 2 pixel rows via driver 13) on page 1, start_tone(rand_range(19,150)), copy_rect_between_pages(1,0, 8,y, 183,y+4) (show it on page 0); then the same sweep from y=179 down to 8 with scroll_rect_down (7200). The rectangles cover the 11x11 tile map view (pixels 8..183). Finally set_draw_page(0) and stop_tone(). The tones give a rumbling noise; sound-disabled machines just see the shake.
notes: 71ca/7200 are the two scroll wrappers for driver entry 13 (negative/positive SI); exact direction mapping not verified.

name: dispatch_command
proto: int dispatch_command(int key)  /* pascal; returns 1 = turn used, 0 = no turn ('What?'), 2 = Talk special */
purpose: The main command dispatcher, called by the three main loops (MAINOUT 8c54 overworld, TOWN 95ee, DUNGEON 8894) with the upper-cased key from read_command_key. Each command prints its name into the message window and calls the overlay implementation; L = g_location (0 overworld, 1..0x20 town, 0x21..0x28 dungeon). ' ': 'Pass\n'; but in the overworld with sails set (g_sail_dir != 0) prints 'Sheets in irons!' and clears g_sail_dir; returns 1. 'A' Attack: MAINOUT_88bc / DUNGEON_9f1a (L>0x20) / TOWN_8bb6, returns their result. 'B' 'Board ' CMDS_c776 (result). 'C' 'Cast...' CAST_cd3a (result). 'D' 'D-What?' 0. 'E': overworld MAINOUT_8aae (result) else 'Enter what?' 1. 'F' 'Fire-' CMDS_ca6a 1. 'G' 'Get-' (name only printed when L<0x21) SJOG_d84e 1. 'H': overworld/dungeon -> hole_up_and_camp (3c9a) 1; town: tile under the party (map_tile_ptr 4402) == 0xab (bed) -> 'Hole up- ' CMDS_c4d2 1 else 'Only in bed!' 1. 'I' 'Ignite torch!' CMDS_cd18 1. 'J' 'Jimmy-' SJOG_ccca 1. 'K': overworld 'Klimb-' CMDS_dba0 1; dungeon DUNGEON_9fe0; town TOWN_8d52 (results). 'L' 'Look': dungeon '...' DNGLOOK_a290 else '-' LOOKOBJ_ac2c, 1. 'M' 'Mix Reagents' CMDS_da58 1. 'N' 'New Order' CMDS_cd5c 1. 'O' 'Open-' SJOG_d2f4 1. 'P': dungeon 'Push\nNot here!' 0 else 'Push-' CMDS_d59a 1. 'Q' 'Quit:' CAST2_f2de 0. 'R' 'Ready...' ZSTATS_f476 1. 'S' 'Search-'/'Search...' SJOG_c8dc 1. 'T': overworld 'Talk-' get_direction; cancelled -> 1 else 'Funny, no response!' 1; town 'Talk-' TALK_c39c -> 2 if it returned nonzero else 1; dungeon 'Talk-Funny, no response!' 1. 'U' 'Use item' CAST_d712 1. 'V' 'View a gem!': if g_gems: gems--, dungeon DNGLOOK_a938 else LOOKOBJ_b38c(x,y), 1; else 'You have none!' 1. 'W' 'W-What?' 0. 'X' 'X-it ' CMDS_ce34 1. 'Y' 'Yell ' CMDS_d398 (result). 'Z' 'Z-stats...' ZSTATS_ec1a 1. 0xfc (Ctrl-B): 'Buffer O' toggles g_flush_after_key, prints 'ff' or 'n', 0. Anything else 'What?' 0.

0x5955.meaning: save 0x3AF direction the sails are set to, 0 lowered

0xa110.name: g_str_commands
0xa110.meaning: command name strings 0xa110..0xa298 ('Buffer O','Sheets in irons!','Pass','Board ','Cast...','D-What?','Enter what?','Fire-','Get-','Hole up- ','Only in bed!','Ignite torch!','Jimmy-','Klimb-','Look','...','Mix Reagents','New Order','Open-','Push','Push-','Quit:','Ready...','Search-','Search...','Talk-','Funny, no response!','Use item','View a gem!','You have none!','W-What?','X-it ','Yell ','Z-stats...','What?')

notes: Return value 0 means the main loop does not advance time.

name: flash_tile_at
proto: void flash_tile_at(int x, int y)  /* pascal: [bp+6]=x, [bp+4]=y */
purpose: Hit/miss flash on a map cell. Outside combat (g_location < 0x80) the world coordinates are converted to view cells: col = x - (g_party_x - 5), row = y - (g_party_y - 5) (the 11x11 view is centred on the party at cell 5,5); in combat the coordinates are already view cells. draw_tile(0, col, row) (tile 0 over the cell), play_random_tones(10,3000,2000), then refresh_map_view (5910) restores the proper tile. Ghidra shows FUN_3522(y,x), e.g. FUN_3522(DAT_5897,DAT_5896) = flash_tile_at(party_x, party_y).
notes: draw_tile(tile,col,row) appears as FUN_10e0(row,col,tile) in Ghidra. Tile 0 is assumed to be the blank/black tile.

name: flash_monster
purpose: Hit flash for a creature. In combat, slot is a g_combat_roster index: the entry's +4 byte is the monster-table slot to draw and, if its flags have 0x80 (a party member), the feedback is instead highlight_party_line(member = entry +3), play_random_tones(0x28,3000,500), un-highlight. Otherwise (and always outside combat, where slot is a monster-table index) draw_tile(0, g_monster_table[slot].x, g_monster_table[slot].y) and play_random_tones(10,3000,2000). Then refresh_map_view (5910). Note outside combat the monster's x,y are used as view cells without conversion (callers are combat/spell code where this is correct).

0xba14.name: g_combat_roster
0xba14.meaning: combat participants (+2 flags, +3 member, +4 monster slot)

0x5c5a.name: g_monster_table
0x5c5a.meaning: save 0x6B4 object/monster table: +0 tile, +1 anim tile, +2 x, +3 y, +4 z, +5 value1, +6 value2, +7 value3; slot 0 = the party/vehicle

name: get_direction
proto: int get_direction(void)  /* returns 1 = direction chosen (g_dx/g_dy set), 0 = cancelled */
purpose:
Prompts for a direction after a command letter. g_dx = g_dy = 0. Reads read_command_key until it is space or a direction code 1..4 (other keys, including Esc, are ignored - the Esc test in the code is unreachable). 1: prints 'West
', g_dx = -1; 2: 'East
', g_dx = +1; 3: 'North
', g_dy = -1; 4: 'South
', g_dy = +1; returns 1. Space: prints 'Pass
' and returns 0. Callers then use g_party_x + g_dx, g_party_y + g_dy as the target cell.

0x5876.name: g_dx
0x5876.meaning: direction delta x (also reused by find_object_at as the found slot index); RAM at save offset 0x2D0

notes: The wiki calls save 0x2D0/0x2D2 monster/PC counts; the code uses them as dx/dy scratch.

name: find_object_at
proto: unsigned char find_object_at(unsigned x, unsigned y, unsigned z)  /* pascal: [bp+8]=x,[bp+6]=y,[bp+4]=z; returns tile or 0, slot in g_dx */
purpose: Scans g_monster_table slots 1..31 (upwards) for an entry with x,y equal to the arguments and, when not in combat (g_location < 0x80), z equal too (in combat the z test is skipped). Returns the entry's base tile (+0) and leaves the slot index in g_dx (0x5876); returns 0 when nothing is found (g_dx then = 32). Slot 0 (the party) is never matched. Ghidra shows FUN_368e(z,y,x); every caller passes g_party_z as z.
notes: empty slots have tile 0 so the 0 return is unambiguous

name: find_object_at_rev
proto: unsigned char find_object_at_rev(unsigned x, unsigned y, unsigned z)  /* pascal; returns tile or 0, slot in g_dx */
purpose: Same search as find_object_at but from slot 31 downwards to slot 0 (the party slot is included), g_dx starting at 31 and decremented; returns the tile of the first match or 0 if none. Used where the topmost (most recently created) object at a cell should win, e.g. monster movement and searching.

name: find_slot_for_tile_offscreen
proto: int find_slot_for_tile_offscreen(char tile)  /* pascal; dead code */
purpose: No callers. Scans g_monster_table from slot 31 down to 0: returns the slot index as soon as it meets an empty slot (tile 0), or a slot whose tile == tile that is either on another level (z != g_party_z) or farther than 5 cells from the party in both x and y; returns -1 if the scan runs out. Looks like an older 'find reusable slot' helper superseded by find_spawn_slot.
notes: dead code; semantics inferred

name: find_slot_with_tile_range
proto: int find_slot_with_tile_range(unsigned lo, unsigned hi, int near_only)  /* pascal: [bp+8]=lo,[bp+6]=hi,[bp+4]=near_only; returns slot 1..23 or 0 */
purpose: Scans g_monster_table slots 1..23 for an entry whose base tile is in [lo,hi] and is not 0xb5; if near_only != 0 the entry must also lie within +-5 cells of the party in both x and y (computed as (byte)(x - g_party_x + 5) <= 10). Returns the first matching slot index, 0 if none. Only called by find_spawn_slot. Ghidra shows FUN_3868(near_only, hi, lo).
notes: slots 24..31 are never considered (reserved for other object kinds)

name: find_spawn_slot
purpose: Chooses a monster-table slot for a new monster/object, evicting an existing entry if necessary, in priority order: an empty slot (tile 0); else a slot within 5 cells of the party holding tiles 1..0xf, then 0x80..0xff, then 0x10..0x11, then 0x30..0x7f; else the same four ranges anywhere; else any slot with tile 0..0xff. Each step is find_slot_with_tile_range(lo,hi,near). Returns the slot (0 only if all 23 slots hold tile 0xb5). Callers (CMDS, LOOKOBJ, MAINOUT, SJOG, TOWN) then fill the slot with set_monster_slot.
notes: 'near first' eviction order inferred from the call sequence; the tile groups are not named.

name: set_town_map_tile
proto: void set_town_map_tile(char tile, unsigned x, unsigned y)  /* pascal: [bp+8]=tile,[bp+6]=x,[bp+4]=y */
purpose: If the party is in a settlement (0 < g_location < 0x21) and tile != 0, writes tile into the in-memory town map at (x,y) via map_tile_ptr (4402). All callers pass (g_door_tile, g_door_x, g_door_y) (save 0x3A9-0x3AB) to put a previously opened door back when it closes or when leaving the map.

0x594f.name: g_door_tile
0x594f.meaning: save 0x3A9 tile of the currently open door

notes: map_tile_ptr(x,y)=4402 appears as FUN_4402(y,x) in Ghidra.

name: find_first_conscious_member
proto: int find_first_conscious_member(void)  /* 0 = found (index in g_dx), 1 = none but someone asleep, -1 = none */
purpose: Scans the party in order; the first member whose status is 'G' or 'P' is stored in g_dx and 0 is returned. Otherwise returns 1 if at least one member is 'S' (asleep - the game can wait for them to wake) or -1 if nobody is available (everyone dead). Used by the main loops to decide whether the party can act / whether the game is over.

name: set_monster_slot
proto: void set_monster_slot(unsigned char tile, unsigned char anim_tile, unsigned char x, unsigned char y, unsigned char z, unsigned char value1, int slot)  /* pascal: slot is the LAST argument ([bp+4]) */
purpose: Fills the first six bytes of g_monster_table[slot]: +0 tile, +1 anim_tile, +2 x, +3 y, +4 z, +5 value1 (value2/value3 at +6/+7 are left untouched). Ghidra lists the parameters reversed, e.g. FUN_3a74(slot,0,0,0,0,0,0) clears a slot and FUN_3a74(slot,0,0,y,x,0,0xe4) is set_monster_slot(0xe4,0,x,y,0,0,slot).
notes: 21 callers

name: rand_0_to
proto: int rand_0_to(int n)  /* pascal; returns rand_range(0, n) */
purpose: Thin wrapper: rand_range(0, n), inclusive of n. Ghidra shows it as void and with extra junk arguments at some call sites; the result in AX is used.

name: random_damage_1_30
purpose: rand_0_to(60) / 2, raised to 1 if 0: a 1..30 damage roll used by traps, spells and combat.

name: animate_wait
purpose: Pause for frames animation frames while keeping the map alive: only if g_map_update_enabled != 0 and frames > 0, repeats frames times { refresh_map_view (5910); wait_ticks(1) }. This is the standard 'pause' used by effects and messages (27 callers use 1 frame, others 2..40).

0x58a4.name: g_map_update_enabled
0x58a4.meaning: save 0x2FE: 1 = update/animate the 2-D map (set when entering/leaving a map), 0 = freeze

name: read_text_line
purpose: Line editor for names, conversation input, shop questions. Saves and clears g_flush_after_key. Loop: key = read_command_key(); Backspace (8) or direction 1 (left) with len > 0: backspace_chars(1), len--; Esc with len > 0: backspace_chars(len), len = 0; printable 0x20..0x7f when len < maxlen: store and echo with put_char; until Enter (0x0d). NUL-terminates buf[len] and restores g_flush_after_key. Input is already upper-cased by read_command_key. Ghidra shows FUN_3b1c(maxlen, buf), e.g. FUN_3b1c(0xc,&0xbd08).
notes: Does not print a newline on Enter.

name: read_number
proto: int read_number(int max_digits)  /* pascal; max_digits clamped to 5 */
purpose: Numeric line editor (used for buying quantities and amounts in CMDS/SHOPPES2). Accepts '0'..'9' while len < max_digits, and '+'/'-' only as the first character; Backspace/left (8/1) and Esc edit as in read_text_line; echoes with put_char. On Enter converts the buffer: digits are summed from the last one backwards times g_pow10_alt[k] (1,10,100,1000,10000 at 0x6a0a); then the first character: '-' negates the total, '+' is ignored, a digit contributes digit*10^k. Returns the value (0 for an empty line).
notes: local buffer is 6 bytes; max_digits > 5 is clamped so it cannot overflow

name: hole_up_and_camp
purpose:
The 'H'ole up command outside towns. Prints 'Hole up & '. If the party vehicle tile (g_monster_table[0].anim_tile, 0x5c5b) is a frigate ((t & 0xf8) == 0x20): prints '
repair...

'; if the frigate tile is <= 0x23 (sails set) prints 'Sails must be
lowered!

', sets g_view_dirty = 1 and returns; otherwise 5 rounds of { MAINOUT_824a (pass a turn), MAINOUT_9c30 (random encounter check); if g_transport_tile & 0xfc != 0x24 (no longer aboard, e.g. combat) return; advance_time (4f7c, 5 minutes) }, then hull += rand_range(1,3) repeatedly until hull >= 10, capped at 99; prints 'Hull now NN!

'; g_view_dirty = 1, g_status_dirty = 1. Else prints 'camp!

': in a town/overworld (g_location < 0x21) the tile under the party is checked: tiles 1..3 (water) -> 'On land or ship!

' return; vehicle tile != 0x1c (not on foot) -> 'On foot!
' return (both set g_view_dirty). Asks 'For how many hours? (1-9) ' (keys '0'..'9' or space; echoes the key and a newline; space or '0' cancel). Counts conscious members ('G'/'P'); if more than one asks 'Wilt thou set a watch? ' Y/N: Yes -> 'Yes' + 'Who will stand guard? Dungeon (g_location > 0x20): g_combat_flags = 6, DNGLOOK_b3c0, DNGLOOK_afce, run_camp_scene (5f86: hours, guard, flags) then select_disk(2), DNGLOOK_b32e, restore monster slot 1 from the backup at 0xaa04 (g_monster_table_backup+8), DUNGEON_8304(0), g_view_dirty = 1. Overworld: camp_outdoors (6360: 60ec(0), 5f86(hours,guard,4), 5e4a), g_view_dirty = 1.
